textbookText: b. Schizogony in liver After the sporozoites are inoculated into the human blood by mosquito, they disappear from blood stream after half an hour and enter hepatic or liver cells. Sporozoites penetrate liver cells with the help of lytic enzymes secreted by paired organelles and multiply there asexually by a process called schizogony. The daughter cells so formed are known as merozoites. Liver schizogony can be discussed in following headings: i. Pre-erythrocytic scizogony (First schizogony in liver cells) After the entry of sporozoite in liver cell, it grows in size and shape, becomes spherical to form schizont. Schizont divides by schizogony (multiple fission) to form thousands of unnucleated cells called cryptomerozoites. Now, liver cells rupture and cryptomerozoites are released into liver sinusoids.
Figure 8.1.16 Schizogony in liver ii. Exo-erythrocytic schizogony (Second schizogony in liver cells)

From liver sinusoids, Cryptomerozoites enter fresh liver cells; grow into circular schizonts which feed on the liver content. They undergo series of schizogony there and finally produce thousands of metacryptomerozoites which are released by the bursting of the liver cells. Metacryptomerozoites are of two types: smaller and more numerous micro-metacryptomerozoites enter blood and attack RBCs. Larger and fewer macro-metacryptomerozoites again attack fresh liver cells.
Do you know? The time period between initial sporozoite infection and first appearance of parasites in blood is called pre-patent period. It is about 8 days in Plasmodium vivax.

c. Schizogony in RBC or erythrocytic schizogony After entering the blood stream, micro-metacryptomerozoites invade RBCs and pass through several stages that are discussed below: i. Micrometacryptomerozoites feed nutrients from RBC; and get vacuolated and rounded to become young trophozoite.

ii. As the trophozoite grows, a central large non-contractile vacuole pushes the nucleus and cytoplasm towards the peiphery. This stage seems to be a ring with a gem like form called signet ring stage. Digestive enzymes of the parasite break down haemoglobin into protein and hematin. Protein is used as food by trophozoite and hematin forms a toxic malarial pigment called haemozoin which is yellowish brown coloured fine granules. iii. The signet ring later develops into amoeboid stage having pseudopodial processes. Small red eosinophilic granules appear in cytoplasm of RBCs called schuffner’s dots and RBC becomes enlarged and pale yellow at this time. iv. Amoeboid stage after active feeding changes into an enlarged and rounded structure called schizont. It undergoes schizogony in which nucleus divides mitotically into 12- 24 nuclei and each remaining in the periphery and surrounded by cytoplasm to form oval shaped merozoites. The peripheral arrangement of the merozoites with central mass of unused cytoplasm, and haemozoin resembles like the arrangement of petals in rose and hence this stage is named as Rosette stage.

The red blood cells rupture to release large number of merozoites in blood plasma. These merozoites, again, attack fresh RBC and finally repeat the cycle in RBC. One Erythrocytic schizogony cycle completes in 48 hours. d) Post erythrocytic schizogony Sometimes, some merozoites may again attack liver cells and undergo schizogony which is referred as post-erythrocytic schizogony.

Figure 8.1.17 Schizogony in RBC Do you know? Release of haemozoin toxin and merozoites to the blood plasma by the rupture of RBC causes malaria fever in which the patient suffers from chills, shivering, high temperature and Biology, Grade 11 | 307
convulsion with profuse sweating. It comes at the interval of every 48 hours i.e at the completion of one erythrocytic cycle which releases merozoites and haemozoin in blood plasma.
Incubation period is the time period between the entry of pathogen and appearance of first symptom. For Plasmodium vivax it is 14 days in average.

e. Formation of gametocytes After the many generations of schizogony in RBCs, some merozoites slowly increase in size producing large amount of haemozoin and transform into specific structures called gametocytes. Gametocytes are of two types: - macrogametocytes and microgametocytes.
Macrogametocytes are called female gametocytes which are less numerous, larger with small compact nucleus and food ladened cytoplasm.
Microgametocytes are called male gametocytes which are more numerous, smaller with clear cytoplasm and large central nucleus.
Questions to think? Why should some merozites be transformed into gametocytes after the many generations of erythrocytic schizogony?

These gametocytes do not develop further but remain inactive in human blood for several weeks. They get either degenerated in human blood or sucked up with blood by female Anopheles mosquito to continue their sexual cycle.
